titlePlain: Automated Isolation as the Last Line,
subtitle: Lesson 16 · Assume Breach: Designing for Containment

eyebrow: Not a new tool, a new question

steps.label: SOAR already does the automation
steps.sub: Isolate a host, disable an account, revoke a token — on a detection

steps.label: The real question is WHEN
steps.sub: Which actions fire first, which wait for a human to approve

steps.label: A design decision, not a tooling one
steps.sub: The platform can automate either path — the review has to choose

eyebrow: The response has a blast radius too

steps.label: One workstation isolated
steps.sub: Worst case: one person, recoverable in minutes

steps.label: One shared service account disabled
steps.sub: Worst case: forty pipelines go down — a self-inflicted outage

steps.label: The dividing line is blast radius
steps.sub: Not detection confidence — the cost of being wrong matters more

code:
AUTO-CONTAIN, no approval:
  single workstation, high-confidence EDR signal
  single session, impossible-travel signal

AUTO-DETECT, human-approved ACTION:
  production server isolation
  shared service account disable
  trusted certificate revocation

SOAR still preps everything instantly either way.
caption: Detect and enrich automatically. Act automatically only where a false positive is cheap.

subtitle: Assume breach, blast radius, and containment now extend to the data and APIs those systems actually protect.
